So I'm taking an online course in Objective C, and the current homework is a program that takes in a value from the user between 1-50 and outputs a grid with "N N^2 N^3 N^4" at the top (see here) and the related values up to the inputted max below. I have the program written already and if I were to submit it I'd surely get a decent grade, but it's not due until Sunday so I started messing around.

I wrote a segment that instead of statically printing the header will do so dynamically based on the number of columns defined by a constant. The problem I'm running into is that it works for only about half the numbers in our given range (1-50). What's really odd is the range is defining the number of rows, not columns. It seems to be putting a random number, or asterisk, or parentheses between the N and the ^; or sometimes just dropping the N entirely. Here is the segment of code I have as it stands, any thoughts would be greatly appreciated!:

const int MAX_COLUMNS = 4;
char notation = 'N';

 for (int col = 0; col < MAX_COLUMNS; col++) {
 if (col == 0) {
 printf("%s%11c", &notation, ' ');
 } else {
 printf("%s^%i%9c", &notation, col + 1, ' ');
 }
 
 }
I can't wrap my head around this bug...
Here are two examples of times when it fails: 50 8

In languages I know, %s is for null-terminated strings. Notation is a char, not a null-terminated string. Try %c instead of %s when printing chars (and drop the &)?

Edit: that is almost certainly the problem. In the "50" example, it's printing "N2", because 50 happens to be the ASCII code for the character "2". In the "8" example, it appears to print nothing because 8 is the ASCII code for backspace (so, it prints the "N", and then moves the cursor back one space; when it prints the ^, the N gets overwritten).

I bet if you choose 65, you'll see "NA", "NA^2", and so on.

Under the hood, your printf is printing whatever it finds in memory starting from the address you gave it, until it finds a byte with value "0". It just so happens that MAX_COLUMNS is located there, so the bytes that make up MAX_COLUMNS get printed as if they were part of the string.
Yup, that was it. I couldn't figure out what it was complaining about and this was the fix. Dropped the & and changed to %c (I had %c and &notation there previously which Xcode complained about).

In your print statements, why did you use %s for a char and then pass a pointer? This seems like the most likely cause to me. Maybe try printf("%c%11c", notation, ' ');

I think that should work. I think what is happening is you are giving printf the address to a char which gets represented as an int, so effectively you are passing an int to be printed as a string. I could be wrong about that though. EDIT: Yeah, I was wrong. Thanks to /u/taxation_is_slavery for pointing this out below.

EDIT: I'd also like to add that you could even do something like: printf("%11c", notation); Although it might mess with the spacing, you might need to increment that value or something but it eliminates the need to pass the space char into the function to get it to space out. There is a width and a length flag and I'm not sure which is being used instead of which in this case, but I do know it's shorter and more efficient.

Actually he was giving the address of that char, but %s format expects null terminated strings, not just a single char, so printf continued until it hit a zero byte somewhere in the memory space after it.

Just starting out, please list your must have add ons
Bagnon is great for sorting loot in a single 'big' backpack so you can sort everything easier.

_NPCScan is great if you are into achievements.

ArkInventory is an amazing bag replacement. You can sort everything into subsections and it has special rules that will take you far beyond the defaults.

Auctioneer is a must have, even if you don't try to profit from the AH.

Bartender if you are like me and need/want a lot of visibility of different spells, professions, and anything else you would normally have to go into your bags/professions/mounts tabs to get after.

Master Plan for garrison missions, but it kind of went down hill after the last upgrade.

PetTracker is good if you play around with battle pets.

Rarity keeps track of attempts to get rare drops.

TomTom is a good waypoint system.

VuhDo is what I use for healing on my Shaman.

WeakAuras is great for tracking casts and CDs but takes a little getting to know.

I also pay for and use Zygors for a bunch of different things.

/u/Defy has a great list; here are a couple more:

1) MyBigIgnite to help you use your combustion dot if you decide to play a fire mage.

2) Movable Holy Power to move and scale the holy power bar if you don't want to use something like weak auras.

3) Some form of boss mod if you choose to raid, either DBM or BigWigs

4) TellMeWhen is fantastic to track cds and buffs if you are raiding.

5) I'll disagree on the use of Bartender and suggest Dominos as a bar re-arranging addon. Bartender creates its own buttons and keybinds that, if broken in an update, will render your character unusable without lots of setup time if you have custom keybinds. Dominos reuses the Blizzard buttons and keybinds so even if the addon is broken in an update, all of your keybinds should still work.

6) Some form of cast bar replacement like Quartz is also nice.

Bartender: Its SO SO useful! You can move your action bars around, change their size, shape and keybinds. I've got it so while I hold down shift it shows new spells and abilities. You should be using your keyboard and not clicking your abilities, its a good habit to get into :P

Deadly Boss Mods (DBM) / BigWigs: Only need one, good for when you start raiding in LFR or seriously raiding and good for some dungeons.

Omen Threat: Good if you're gonna start tanking so you can tell who has aggro

Recount: If you're into bragging how much dps (damage per second) you do in dungeons, this is for you.

If you ever get into the PvP aspect of the game (which can be quite intimidating for new players since it's an established scene now, which has been competitive for almost eight years now), I would suggest the following addons to make your experience a little easier:

-InterruptBar - It shows you the cooldown of enemy player interrupts, which make you unable to cast your abilities if they manage to use them as you are casting a spell

-Gladius - It is a UI showing you the Diminishing Return counter of your Crowd Control effects on the enemy, and is highly customizable to your needs (If you're not sure what crowd control and diminishing returns, or CC and DR are, please go Here to find out more. It also has a trinket timer for enemy players.

-GladiatorLosSA: Now this one is really controversial for a lot of the arena-junkies in this game, but this addon is so strong that it should have been banned a long time ago: Anytime an enemy casts a major spell or uses a major ability (like blade storm or divine shield), a voice will tell you the ability that is being cast. A lot of people frown upon this addon because it really takes away from your gamesense as it makes you dependent on the addon to be able to tell when sticky situations are underway, but it makes it almost impossible for a player with a working set of ears to miss anything you're doing.

For BGs, there are really only two must-have addons:

-Healers must die: This addon will put a raid-frame style symbol above your healers and enemy healers, making it easier to spot them and target them down in BGs.

-BattlegroundTargets: It gives you a list of all the enemy players in a BG, as well as their class, specialization, and current health. Very useful, especially in rated BGs.

A thread to talk about all things EarthBound/MOTHER!

Earthbound is a game that somehow managed to evoke nostalgia from me despite having never played it. There I was last year, 24 years old, experiencing this venerable artifact of Nintendo, and it was immediately a heartfelt connection. I could see how it shaped pokemon, a series that raised me, and I loved the quirky, sometimes subtly mature humor. It's a game I refuse to rate on a scale of 1-10; it just is. It's an experience. It's sincere. It's what happens when one man is given the resources to bare his soul through story.
Mother 3 has to have the heaviest story and ending I've ever seen. If you can avoid crying at the end you're a stronger man than I am.
I've only played Mother 2 so far and I loved the game. I was planning to play Mother 3 soon, but would it be wise to play Mother 1 first?
I have never played any of the MOTHER/Earthbound games. But I hear they are good. Should I give them a try?

Yes, you should play it. It is a unique experience unlike any game I have ever played. I don't want to spoil anything by giving details, just play the SNES game first (don't get discouraged by the initial grinding...it goes away after the first town).

I play Earthbound every 5-6 years. It was one of the first SNES RPG's I got into. One of the things I liked the best about it was how similar it was to real life. You eat pizza, burgers, go to jazz shows, and wander department stores.

Honestly from a gaming perspective, pretty weak. Really grindy, relatively boring puzzles, and too much fetch quest for an rpg that is so bare bones. But I guess the reality is that it must be looked at as a whole. It's late eighties/ early nineties nostalgia/satire/commentary mixed with absurdism. It hits a lot of notes that could resonate with people familiar with the culture of the time.

I wouldn't recommend it to the youth, but someone a little bit older could find a lot of meaning in it, if they can suffer the archaic gameplay long enough to let the art sink in
